questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Arrange the following alkyl bromides in decreasing order of their rate of SN2 reaction with iodide ion in acetone: (A) 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane (B) Bromomethane (C) 2-Bromopropane (D) Bromoethane.
questions.explanation: In SN2 the nucleophile attacks from the back of the carbon, so crowding at that carbon slows the reaction. The reactivity order is methyl greater than primary, greater than secondary, greater than tertiary. Bromomethane reacts fastest, then bromoethane, then 2-bromopropane, and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane barely reacts by SN2.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Nucleophilic substitution (SN2) and steric effects

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about nucleophilic substitution of haloalkanes. I. An SN2 reaction of a chiral haloalkane proceeds with inversion of configuration. II. An SN1 reaction of a chiral haloalkane gives a nearly racemic product. III. Tertiary haloalkanes react mainly by SN2 with strong nucleophiles such as hydroxide ion. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: SN2 is a single concerted step with backside attack, which inverts the configuration at the carbon. SN1 proceeds through a planar carbocation that the nucleophile can attack from either face, giving near racemisation. Tertiary carbons are too crowded for SN2, so they react by SN1 or by elimination with strong bases.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Mechanisms of SN1 and SN2 reactions

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: 2-Bromobutane is heated with alcoholic potassium hydroxide. Which alkene is the major product?
questions.explanation: Alcoholic KOH removes HBr by elimination. Following the Saytzeff rule, the proton is lost from the carbon that gives the more substituted and more stable alkene. The internal alkene but-2-ene, which is disubstituted, therefore predominates over the terminal but-1-ene.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Dehydrohalogenation and the Saytzeff rule

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Finkelstein reaction (B) Swarts reaction (C) Wurtz reaction (D) Dow process. List-II: (I) Sodium metal in dry ether (II) Sodium iodide in dry acetone (III) Silver fluoride or mercurous fluoride (IV) Sodium hydroxide at about 623 K and high pressure, followed by acidification. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: The Finkelstein reaction exchanges chlorine or bromine for iodine using NaI in acetone, and the insoluble NaCl drives the change. The Swarts reaction uses AgF or Hg2F2 to introduce fluorine. Wurtz coupling joins two alkyl halides with sodium in dry ether, and the Dow process converts chlorobenzene to phenol with NaOH at high temperature and pressure.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Methods of preparation; conversion of chlorobenzene to phenol

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Ethylmagnesium bromide is treated with water. The organic product is:
questions.explanation: Grignard reagents are strong bases and take a proton from water, so the ethyl group becomes an alkane. The C-Mg bond is replaced by a C-H bond, which gives ethane. Ethanol would form only if the Grignard reagent reacted with a carbonyl compound or with oxygen.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Reaction of haloalkanes with magnesium (Grignard reagents)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Assertion (A): Chlorobenzene does not undergo nucleophilic substitution with aqueous sodium hydroxide under ordinary conditions. Reason (R): In chlorobenzene the C-Cl bond has partial double-bond character due to resonance, and the sp2-hybridised carbon attached to chlorine is more electronegative.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: The lone pair on chlorine conjugates with the ring, which shortens the C-Cl bond and gives it partial double-bond character, making it harder to break. The sp2 carbon is also more electronegative than an sp3 carbon, so it holds the bonding electrons more tightly. Together these effects explain why chlorobenzene resists nucleophilic substitution under ordinary conditions.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Nature of the C-X bond in haloarenes

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about polyhalogen compounds. I. DDT is persistent in the environment and accumulates in the fatty tissues of organisms. II. Chlorofluorocarbons (freons) release chlorine free radicals in the stratosphere that catalyse the breakdown of ozone. III. Freons are chemically reactive in the lower atmosphere, which is why they are used as refrigerants. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: DDT is a persistent organochlorine pesticide that is stored in fatty tissue, which is why its use was restricted. Freons are chemically inert in the lower atmosphere, so they reach the stratosphere, where UV light releases chlorine radicals that destroy ozone. Their inertness, not reactivity, is the reason they serve as refrigerants, so statement III is false.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Polyhalogen compounds (DDT and freons)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Which of the following monosaccharides is a ketose?
questions.explanation: Fructose has a ketone group (C=O) at C-2, so it is a ketohexose. Glucose, galactose and mannose each have an aldehyde group at C-1 and are aldohexoses.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Carbohydrates

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: On hydrolysis, sucrose gives which pair of monosaccharides?
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide of alpha-D-glucose and beta-D-fructose joined by a glycosidic bond. Hydrolysis breaks this bond and releases one glucose and one fructose, which is why the mixture is called invert sugar.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Carbohydrates

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar. Which feature of its structure explains this?

options.text: It has a free aldehyde group at C-1 of its glucose unit
It exists only in the open-chain ketose form
The glycosidic bond joins the anomeric carbons of glucose and fructose, so no free aldehyde or ketone group can form
It contains no hydroxyl groups at all

questions.explanation: In sucrose, C-1 of alpha-glucose is joined to C-2 of beta-fructose, so neither anomeric carbon is free to open into a carbonyl group. Reducing sugars need a free aldehyde or ketone, or a ring that can open to one, to reduce Fehling's or Tollens' reagent.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Carbohydrates

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: How does amylopectin differ structurally from amylose?

options.text: It is made of beta-D-glucose units joined by beta-1,4 linkages
It is made of fructose units joined by alpha-1,2 linkages
It is an unbranched chain of alpha-1,4 linkages
It has alpha-1,6 glycosidic branch points in addition to alpha-1,4 linkages

questions.explanation: Both are polymers of alpha-D-glucose. Amylose is essentially a linear chain of alpha-1,4 linkages, while amylopectin is branched at alpha-1,6 linkages.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Carbohydrates

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Cellulose is a polymer of which monosaccharide, and what linkage joins its units?

options.text: Beta-D-glucose units joined by beta-1,4 glycosidic linkages
Alpha-D-glucose units joined by alpha-1,4 glycosidic linkages
Beta-D-fructose units joined by beta-1,2 glycosidic linkages
Alpha-D-galactose units joined by alpha-1,6 glycosidic linkages

questions.explanation: Cellulose is an unbranched chain of beta-D-glucose units linked by beta-1,4 bonds. The beta linkage keeps the chains straight so they pack into strong fibres, and humans cannot digest it because they lack an enzyme that hydrolyses beta-glycosidic bonds.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Carbohydrates

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Glycogen is the storage polysaccharide of animals. It is structurally most similar to which polysaccharide?
questions.explanation: Glycogen is a highly branched polymer of alpha-D-glucose, like amylopectin, but it branches more often, roughly every 8 to 12 residues. Cellulose is linear and beta-linked, and amylose is essentially unbranched.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Carbohydrates

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: In aqueous solution at its isoelectric point, glycine exists mainly as which species?
questions.explanation: An amino acid exists as a zwitterion, carrying a protonated amino group and a deprotonated carboxylate group. At the isoelectric point the net charge is zero, and the dominant form of glycine is the zwitterion H3N+-CH2-COO-.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Proteins

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: In the alpha-helix, the secondary structure of a protein is stabilised mainly by which interaction?

options.text: Ionic bonds between arginine and aspartate side chains
Van der Waals forces between adjacent helices
Hydrogen bonds between the C=O of one residue and the N-H of the residue four positions along the chain

questions.explanation: In an alpha-helix, each backbone C=O group hydrogen-bonds with the N-H group of the amino acid four residues ahead, which holds the coil together. Disulfide bonds and salt bridges between side chains stabilise tertiary structure, not secondary structure.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Proteins

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: When a protein is denatured by heat or a change in pH, which structural levels are generally lost?
questions.explanation: Denaturation disrupts the hydrogen bonds, salt bridges and disulfide bonds that maintain secondary and tertiary structure, so the chain unfolds. The sequence of amino acids (primary structure) and the peptide bonds linking them stay intact.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Proteins

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Which statement about enzymes is correct?

options.text: Enzymes are consumed in the reaction they catalyse
Enzymes are highly specific for their substrates
Enzymes change the equilibrium constant of the reaction
Enzymes are most active at very high temperatures

questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts with high substrate specificity. They lower the activation energy, are not consumed, and do not change the equilibrium constant. Their activity falls at very high temperatures because the protein denatures.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Enzymes

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Match List-I (vitamin) with List-II (deficiency disease). List-I: (A) Vitamin B1 (B) Vitamin C (C) Vitamin D (D) Vitamin K. List-II: (I) Rickets (II) Scurvy (III) Beriberi (IV) Delayed blood clotting. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Vitamin B1 deficiency causes beriberi (III). Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy (II). Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets in children (I). Vitamin K deficiency delays blood clotting (IV), so the correct pairing is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV).
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Vitamins

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Which vitamin is synthesised in the human skin when it is exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: A precursor (7-dehydrocholesterol) in the skin is converted to vitamin D3 by ultraviolet light from sunlight. Vitamin C is not synthesised by humans and must come from food such as citrus fruit.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Vitamins
